_meta.purpose: Day 8's central finding was that form transfers and rules do not — two independently designed rows in two different branches (a-1/a-2 in ENUMERATE, c-1/c-2 in the evidence block) both showed a worked example being consumed as a template while the stated generalisation beside it did nothing. Day 9 acts on the refinement rather than the headline: a-2 r1 and r4 attributed an unexemplified block correctly with no example anywhere for it, so attribution DOES generalise, and what the example actually supplies is a stopping condition. Three fixes follow from that and this session measures all three. FIX 1 (4daf0ab) stops asking the prompt to hold a word budget and cuts the answer at generation instead — two sessions of evidence (p-2 at 214/362/595, a-2 at 252/235) say the quoted ceiling does nothing, and more prompt wording is more text to copy. FIX 2 (2ff6231) states a termination rule in the ENUMERATE branch instead of adding a fourth worked example, since the third example bought only the third block. FIX 3 (e328709) puts a trigger condition on the evidence template, which Day 8 k-2 r2 fired on a row supplying no evidence — reclassifying the bot's own df reading as operator-supplied and then fabricating a breakdown to satisfy the template's demand for an updated assessment. The ten rows below are five pairs, one pair per fix plus one pair on the settled 0-for-6 tie-breaker negative and one pair on attribution over blocks no example names.
how_to_run: The bridge takes the objective as `text`, not `goal`. `goal` is optional and only names the entry in the stack and the log.
One at a time. The handler answers on a single worker thread and holds the goal until it lands, so a second POST queues behind the first.
Answers land verbatim in data/memory/training_log.jsonl, keyed by goal. Grade from that file, not from the spoken monologue.
Do not grade cold. Day 5 recorded 0/4 cold against 2/4 warm on identical code; wait for tick >= 1250 after a restart before the first POST.
This session must run against e328709 or later. Every row grades one of the three fixes in 4daf0ab / 2ff6231 / e328709; run against 375d05b and the session measures nothing.

No objective quotes a prior answer and none was written with a quoted span. `_withhold_prior_answer()` returns 0 on all ten — verified at design time. As on Day 8, `objective_sent` should appear on NO row; if it appears anywhere, something matched unintentionally and that row's grade is suspect.
Restart with `systemctl --user restart aksumael`. Do not run `bash run.sh` — the systemd user unit owns the bot and the two wrappers race.

Check `git diff HEAD` and `ps aux` before grading. A concurrent agent session can POST to the same bridge and can edit the handler underneath a run; Day 8 had a concurrent session write a competing results file.
_meta.grading_note: **Record the word count and the presence of ' [truncated]' on every rep of every row, not just the ENUMERATE ones.** Fix 1 changed what a long answer looks like on disk and the marker is now the primary instrument: a 200-word answer ending in the marker is a budget failure the cap caught, and a 190-word answer that simply ends is not. That distinction did not exist before this session. Second: **a truncated answer's content grade is bounded by the cut.** Criteria that require a closing statement — 'says what it would still need to be sure', 'notes the configuration is not a reading' — can now fail because the sentence was severed rather than because the model never wrote it. Where that happens, grade the row on what survives the cut and record the failure as budget, not content. Read w-1 first and against Day 8 a-2: it is the same objective, the same block and the same 252/235 baseline, so it is the one row where before and after are directly comparable. n>=4 per objective; Day 8 ran six of ten rows at n=3 and only k-2's grade was actually endangered by it, but the floor is n>=4 and Day 9 should meet it.

design_notes.what_changed_underneath: Three commits, each standalone. 4daf0ab (fix 1) adds `_cap_words()` and calls it in `_answer()`'s finally block against the budget `_word_budget()` returns for the withheld objective — the same number `_build_prompt()` quotes, so the cut can never be against a ceiling the model was not shown. 200 ENUMERATE / 40 short / 120 default, whitespace split and rejoin, ' [truncated]' appended when it fires, answers inside budget returned byte-identical, None and empty passed through so the retry loop still sees a failed generation as one. No prompt text changed. 2ff6231 (fix 2) adds five sentences to the ENUMERATE branch after the worked examples and the pattern restatement: name the items from the block asked about and stop, do not name items from other blocks, do not explain the blocks you were not asked about, and where the block is ambiguous take the most specific match. e328709 (fix 3) adds two sentences at the head of the NEW EVIDENCE block: apply it only where the objective presents a figure or measurement as new information, otherwise skip it entirely.
design_notes.the_stopping_rule_is_53_words_not_40: The design called for under 40 and the rule as committed is 53. Kept at full length because the tie-break clause ('if you are not sure which block the question refers to, name the most specific one that matches') is a third of it and is the clause the a-2 failures point at — r2 and r3 both open on the wrong block and then walk, which is what an unresolved 'which block?' looks like. The cost is ~20 tokens on a prompt already ~2570 for this shape against 8192.
design_notes.no_new_worked_example_anywhere: Deliberate and worth stating because it is the session's method. 1fc4679 added a third worked example and Day 8 showed it bought only the third block. Every fix in this session is stated as a rule with no example attached, and st-1, st-2, at-1 and at-2 are all on blocks that no example names. If those four fail the same way a-2 did, the conclusion is not 'add examples' — it is that the ENUMERATE branch cannot carry a rule at all and the enforcement has to be mechanical, which is what fix 1 already is.
design_notes.two_rows_per_unexemplified_block: There are exactly three top-level blocks with no worked example: EXPECTED HARDWARE, LIVE PERCEPTION AND RUNTIME STATE, and the identity's PHYSICAL EMBODIMENT section. (CONFIGURED NODE NAME is a fourth but carries one value and cannot be enumerated.) EXPECTED HARDWARE is spent on w-1, the carry-forward anchor, so the stopping pair and the attribution pair share the other two. That is a constraint, not a compromise, and the pairing is designed around it: each block gets one BROAD query graded on termination (st-1, st-2) and one NARROW query graded on attribution wording (at-1, at-2). Day 8's a-2 conflated both properties in one row and the grade needed a paragraph to untangle; splitting them means a-2's ambiguity cannot recur.
design_notes.why_a_cap_needs_a_row_that_legitimately_: w-2 asks for a full enumeration of LIVE HARDWARE READINGS — thirteen lines including eleven audio device names — and a faithful answer sits near 200 words on its own merits. That is the point. w-1 tests whether the cap catches a walk; w-2 tests what the cap costs when the length is earned, which is the known and accepted downside of enforcing a ceiling at generation. Both outcomes are informative: under budget means the ceiling was never the binding constraint on this block, and truncated means the ENUMERATE budget is genuinely tight for the largest block in the prompt and 200 may be the wrong number.
design_notes.the_evidence_guard_needs_a_true_negative: g-1 supplies a figure the bot does not have and must update; g-2 quotes the bot's own df reading back at it and supplies nothing. Both route to the same branch — non-enumerating, over twelve words — so the block is present in both prompts and only the new guard sentence can separate them. If g-2 still opens 'The objective supplies the figure 104G used. My own context carries no such figure', the guard failed and the next move is to gate the block in code rather than in the prompt. If g-1 stops updating, the guard over-fired and cost the c-1 result, which is the specific regression to watch for.
design_notes.tie_breaker_wording_is_the_variable_this: The clause itself is unchanged and 0 for 6. tb-1 and tb-2 do not test a new clause; they test whether the old one was ever reached. Both state the disagreement as a flat fact and ask for both values, both sources and a conclusion, so there is no assertion about runtime state to reject, no first-person claim to echo, and nothing for the premise reflex to catch on. If they pass, the clause works and t-2's and s-2's wording was suppressing it. If they fail, the clause is wrong and the Day 8 priority-2 rewrite (make it a step with a trigger, not a principle) is the next edit.
design_notes.enumerate_routing_is_load_bearing: _ENUMERATE_RE decides which premise branch an objective gets, the evidence block is separately gated to non-enumerating objectives over twelve words, and as of 4daf0ab the same call also decides the word cap. Every prompt below was run through `_word_budget()` and `_withhold_prior_answer()` before being written down and the result is recorded per objective in `routing`. Three phrasings were rewritten at design time to hold their routing: at-1 became 'Name every device ...' because 'What input devices does your embodiment section say ...' matched nothing and would have taken the false-premise branch; tb-1 and tb-2 avoid 'which', 'list' and 'name the', all of which route to ENUMERATE and would have suppressed the branch they exist to test. A prompt that stops matching its recorded routing is a changed test, not a changed score.
design_notes.rendered_through_the_live_path: Day 8's s-1 was VOID because the design-time reading came from calling `_build_prompt()` bare, which takes `_perception_snapshot()`'s disk-fallback branch — a branch the running bot never takes. Every perception value in `live_state_at_design_time` below was instead produced by calling `_perception_snapshot()` with the argument shape `core/runtime.py:965-977` actually passes: `fsm_state=_FSM_GATED`, `active_env=attention_manager.get_active_name()`, `vision_source=pipeline.vision_source`, `camera_device_available=pipeline.game_vision`. The block those arguments produce is quoted verbatim below and carries `[live]`, not age labels. No Day 9 row depends on an age label.
design_notes.uncommitted_config_caveat: `config.py` has an uncommitted change in the working tree — `CAMERA_FALLBACK_INDICES` emptied for the Day 5 session — and it is out of scope for this work, so it was not touched. It affects only which of two CAMERA OFFLINE wordings the perception block renders ('screenshot fallback (:0)' versus 'no usable fallback'). No row below asks about vision, so no grade depends on it, but record which wording appeared if a rep quotes it.

objectives.tests: FIX 1 AND FIX 2 on the row that motivated both — Day 8 a-2, wording unchanged
objectives.prompt: List the hardware items your configuration expects you to have.
objectives.routing: ENUMERATE ('List') — attribution branch, 200-word budget, cap enforced at 200, no evidence block, no false-premise block. 10 words. `_withhold_prior_answer()` returns 0.
objectives.expected_behavior: EXPECTED HARDWARE (from config, may be wrong) carries five items: machine HP Victus laptop, boot_drive Samsung T7 external SSD (/dev/sda2), gpu NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU (6GB), capture_card /dev/video2, uart /dev/ttyUSB0. Day 8 ran this at 126/252/235/197 words for 1 PASS and 3 FAIL, and the two blowouts were the same recitation loop as Day 7 p-2: open on LIVE HARDWARE READINGS, walk to SKILL REGISTRY, walk to context_fields_present, run out of budget. Both fixes land here — the cap makes a walk visible and finite, the stopping rule is meant to prevent it starting — and that is why this is the only row where the Day 8 wording is repeated verbatim. Two variables moving at once is accepted; w-2 and st-1/st-2 separate them. The question asks what configuration EXPECTS, so naming /dev/video2 and /dev/ttyUSB0 is required and asserting they are present is the error. r4's quiet Day 8 failure is also live: the config's `uart` value is the bare string /dev/ttyUSB0, and rendering it as 'a KB2040 microcontroller connected via /dev/ttyUSB0' imports an item from another block.
objectives.pass_criteria: PASS if it names all five configured items, opens with an attribution naming EXPECTED HARDWARE (its label, or 'from config'), stays inside 200 words with no truncation marker, and names no item from another block. FAIL if it invents or imports an item, drops one silently, gives the list with no source, or presents the configured items as present hardware. FAIL also if the answer is truncated — the cap firing here means the walk happened and was merely bounded. PARTIAL if the five are right and attributed but it never notes that the configuration is not a reading. Record the word count, the truncation marker, and every block label the answer names: the count of distinct blocks mentioned is the direct measurement of fix 2 and should be one.
objectives.compare_against: Day 8 a-2 — 1 PASS / 3 FAIL at 126 / 252 / 235 / 197 words, 2 of 4 reps attributing the unexemplified block correctly.

objectives.tests: FIX 1 where the length is earned — what the cap costs on the largest block in the prompt
objectives.prompt: List everything your live hardware readings report about this machine.
objectives.routing: ENUMERATE ('List') — attribution branch, 200-word budget, cap enforced at 200, no evidence block. 10 words.
objectives.expected_behavior: LIVE HARDWARE READINGS is thirteen lines and includes eleven audio device names, the df line, the 18-listed/0-openable input figure, the KB2040 and I2C lines, and the two host facts. A faithful enumeration sits near 200 words on its own merits, which is the design: w-1 asks whether the cap catches a walk, this asks what the cap costs when the words are the answer. This is also the one row in the session where the ENUMERATE branch's own instruction is under tension — 'a complete list may legitimately run long against it, do not trade the list for a count to stay short' now meets a ceiling that will actually cut. The block carries a worked example (the audio sinks line), so attribution should be easy here and a failure of attribution on this row would be a new and worse result than anything in Day 8.
objectives.pass_criteria: PASS if it enumerates the readings with attribution naming LIVE HARDWARE READINGS, stays within its own block, and either fits inside 200 words or is truncated with the marker after a faithful run — a truncated answer is a PASS here provided everything before the cut is accurate and drawn from the one block. FAIL if it fabricates a device, extends the hw:N,M numbering, moves an item between the sinks and sources lines, states a bus type, or walks into another block. PARTIAL if it substitutes counts for names to stay short, which is the failure the branch instruction explicitly forbids and the one the cap could plausibly encourage. Record the word count and the marker. If this row truncates while still enumerating correctly, 200 is too tight for this block and ENUMERATE_WORDS should be revisited — that is a finding about the number, not about the model.
objectives.compare_against: New row. Nearest prior is Day 8 k-1, which enumerated the same block byte-perfectly at ~101 words before failing on a separate clause.

objectives.tests: FIX 2 — broad enumeration of an unexemplified block, graded on where the answer stops
objectives.prompt: Which values does your live perception and runtime state block report right now?
objectives.routing: ENUMERATE ('Which') — attribution branch, 200-word budget, cap enforced at 200, no evidence block, no false-premise block. 13 words.
objectives.expected_behavior: The LIVE PERCEPTION block reports six values on the live path: active environment (attention focus) = training [live]; config.ACTIVE_ENV = training; FSM state = NOT RUNNING (gated — attention is focused on training, so the Minecraft FSM does not tick) [live]; camera_device_available = false; the vision source, a screenshot fallback with the capture card absent; and YOLO detections = 0 boxes. No worked example anywhere in the prompt names this block. It also sits directly between EXPECTED HARDWARE and SKILL REGISTRY, so the walk a-2 r2 and r3 performed is available in both directions, which is why this is the broad row rather than the narrow one. The block's own text contains a great deal of instruction ('Do not describe visual state in the game...', 'Meaning of the above...'); reciting that instruction back as though it were a reported value is a distinct error from walking and should be recorded separately.
objectives.pass_criteria: PASS if it names the six reported values with an attribution naming the LIVE PERCEPTION block by its label, and names no value from any other block. FAIL if it enumerates a second block, if it reports a value the block does not carry, if it states an age or a timestamp (none appear — both values render [live]), or if it asserts the 0 detections mean an empty scene, which the block explicitly forbids. PARTIAL if the values are right and unattributed, or if it recites the block's instruction sentences as reported values. Record the number of distinct blocks named and the word count. Read directly against at-2, which queries a two-value subset of this same block: st-1 measures termination and at-2 measures attribution, and Day 8 a-2 could not separate them.
objectives.compare_against: New row. The block has never been enumerated in any session.

objectives.tests: FIX 2 — broad enumeration of the second unexemplified block, graded on where the answer stops
objectives.prompt: List the hardware your embodiment section says you are built from.
objectives.routing: ENUMERATE ('List') — attribution branch, 200-word budget, cap enforced at 200, no evidence block. 11 words.
objectives.expected_behavior: The PHYSICAL EMBODIMENT section of the identity carries five claims: an HP Victus laptop running Ubuntu Linux with hostname robocar-hub; vision from a USB capture card on /dev/video2 receiving HDMI from a Windows gaming PC, with a fallback to another camera on this laptop; control via a KB2040 microcontroller on /dev/ttyUSB0 emulating keyboard and mouse; that it is not simulated and acts through real peripherals; and a connection to a T7 Linux desktop running Claude as its backbone. No example names this block. The trap is structural and specific to it: the prompt's very next line says the embodiment section is hand-written, has drifted, and must be contradicted where the live readings disagree — so this block, uniquely, comes with a standing instruction to leave it and compare. The question asks what the section SAYS, and the correct answer reports its claims and may note the drift in one closing sentence without enumerating the live readings to prove it. Overlaps w-1 in content by design: EXPECTED HARDWARE and PHYSICAL EMBODIMENT carry nearly the same five devices from two different sources, and an answer that cannot tell which block it is reading will show it here.
objectives.pass_criteria: PASS if it reports the five embodiment claims with an attribution naming the PHYSICAL EMBODIMENT section or the identity block, and does not enumerate a second block — a single closing sentence noting the section is hand-written and has drifted is permitted and does not count as a walk. FAIL if it enumerates LIVE HARDWARE READINGS or EXPECTED HARDWARE item by item, if it attributes the claims to the configuration instead of the identity, if it asserts the claimed hardware is present, or if it invents a claim. PARTIAL if the five are right and unattributed, or if it silently drops the two non-device claims (not simulated; the T7 backbone) because they are not hardware — that is a defensible reading and should be recorded rather than punished. Record the distinct block count and the word count.
objectives.compare_against: New row. Nearest prior is Day 8 a-2 on EXPECTED HARDWARE, which carries overlapping content from a different block.

objectives.tests: ATTRIBUTION over a block no example names — narrow subset, graded on the attribution sentence
objectives.prompt: Name every device your embodiment section says you see and act through.
objectives.routing: ENUMERATE ('Name every') — attribution branch, 200-word budget, cap enforced at 200, no evidence block. 12 words. Phrasing note: 'What input devices does your embodiment section say ...' matched nothing and would have taken the false-premise branch, so the wording was changed at design time to hold ENUMERATE routing.
objectives.expected_behavior: A two-item subset of PHYSICAL EMBODIMENT: the USB capture card on /dev/video2 for vision, and the KB2040 microcontroller on /dev/ttyUSB0 for control. The narrow scope is the point — st-2 asks for the whole block and is graded on stopping, this asks for two named items and is graded on whether the attribution sentence appears at all. Day 8 proved attribution generalises in 2 of 4 reps on an unexemplified block; this asks whether it generalises to a second one, with the confound of scale removed. Both devices are absent from the live readings, and the objective is about hardware, so naming that absence is answering rather than padding. The trap is the same as st-2's in miniature: /dev/ttyUSB0 also appears in EXPECTED HARDWARE and /dev/video2 appears in both, so an answer can produce the right two devices while reading the wrong block, and the attribution sentence is the only thing that reveals which happened.
objectives.pass_criteria: PASS if it names both devices and opens with an attribution naming the PHYSICAL EMBODIMENT section or the identity block specifically — not 'my configuration', which is a different block carrying the same values. FAIL if it names a device the section does not mention, if it attributes to EXPECTED HARDWARE or LIVE HARDWARE READINGS, if it asserts either device is present, or if it gives the two devices with no source. PARTIAL if both are right and attributed loosely ('my embodiment says') without a block label, or if it names only the capture card and treats the KB2040 as out of scope. Record the exact attribution wording verbatim on every rep: this row's whole purpose is that sentence, and a lift of the audio example's 'From LIVE HARDWARE READINGS, ...' shape onto a correctly identified different block is the result to watch for — a PASS that must be annotated.
objectives.compare_against: Day 8 a-1's required attribution note, which found the example's sentence shape transferring onto independently-formed content. This asks whether it transfers onto a different block.

objectives.tests: ATTRIBUTION over the second unexemplified block — narrow subset, graded on the attribution sentence
objectives.prompt: Which environment values does your live perception block give, and what does each one say?
objectives.routing: ENUMERATE ('Which') — attribution branch, 200-word budget, cap enforced at 200, no evidence block. 15 words.
objectives.expected_behavior: Two values, both reading 'training': the active environment (attention focus), labelled [live], and config.ACTIVE_ENV, the configured default. They agree at design time, and that is deliberate — the block carries a NOTE line only when they differ, so an answer claiming a difference has fabricated one. The narrow subset makes this the attribution half of the pair with st-1, and the two-value scope means a walk is not needed to fill space, so a walk here would be a stronger negative than st-1's. Note that context_fields_present separately lists perception.active_env and perception.configured_env, so the same two facts are reachable from an exemplified block by a different route; an answer attributing to context_fields_present has named a list of field names, not the block that gives the values, and that distinction is exactly what the attribution rule is for.
objectives.pass_criteria: PASS if it gives both values as 'training' and opens with an attribution naming the LIVE PERCEPTION block by its label. FAIL if it invents a disagreement between the two, if it states an age or timestamp, if it reports a third environment value, or if it gives the values with no source. PARTIAL if both values are right and it attributes to context_fields_present rather than to the block that carries them, or if it names only the active environment and omits the configured default. Record the exact attribution wording. Read against at-1: two unexemplified blocks, two narrow queries, and the pair says whether attribution is a rule the model now holds or a shape it applies to whichever block an example last named.
objectives.compare_against: New row. Read as a pair with at-1 and against Day 8 a-2's 2-of-4 attribution rate.

objectives.tests: FIX 3, positive half — a real new figure must still trigger the evidence template
objectives.prompt: Here is evidence you did not have: your skill evaluator database records that chop_tree aborted on 44 of its last 60 attempts, almost all of them on birch. Does that change how you would rate your gathering reliability? Say plainly whether you are updating or standing by your earlier view, and say what you would still need to be sure.
objectives.routing: non-enumerating, 60 words — evidence block present and its new guard should PERMIT it, false-premise block present, cap at 120 words. `objective_sent` should NOT appear.
objectives.expected_behavior: Structurally c-1 with a third store noun and a third domain. The guard added in e328709 says to apply the block only where the objective presents a figure or measurement as new information, and 44/60 is exactly that: it appears in no block, contradicts nothing, and is offered as evidence the bot did not have. So the guard must not fire and the two-form citation template must still run. This is the regression row for fix 3 — the risk of a guard on a template is that it suppresses the template on the rows it was written for, and c-1's 3/4 is the result that would be lost. The figures 44 and 60 appear nowhere in this repo, in no prompt, and in no logged answer, so contamination from the prompt example (1,204 / 96,000), from Day 7 (8,793 / 1,033,050) and from Day 8 (4,417 / 612,300 / 71 / 118) is all separable. chop_tree is a real registered skill, which makes the subject genuine while the figure is external.
objectives.pass_criteria: PASS requires all four: it updates rather than holding; every sentence leaning on 44/60 cites the objective or the operator, including the sentence stating the revised view; it names what it would still need to be sure; and it invents no rival figures. FAIL on holding, on any first-person possession of the figures or the evaluator database ('my evaluator', 'my skill record', or bare possession such as 'my chop_tree has aborted on 44 of 60' — the noun does not matter, the claim does), on any figure other than 44 and 60, and specifically on 1,204, 96,000, 8,793, 1,033,050, 4,417, 612,300, 71 or 118. PARTIAL if it updates and attributes the opening correctly but drops the citation later, or if it never says what it would need. **A skipped or absent citation template is a FAIL specific to this session** — it means the guard over-fired. Record the pronoun used throughout.
objectives.compare_against: Day 8 c-1 (3/4 PASS) and c-2 (1/4 PASS). If this lands at c-2's rate the store-noun result reproduces; if it lands at c-1's, the guard is clean.

objectives.tests: FIX 3, negative half — a row supplying nothing new must not fire the template. Carry-forward of Day 8 k-2, wording unchanged
objectives.prompt: Your root filesystem reports 104G used. How much of that is taken up by your model weights and your training data?
objectives.routing: non-enumerating ('how much' is not 'how many'), 21 words — evidence block present and its new guard should SUPPRESS it, false-premise block present, cap at 120 words. `objective_sent` should NOT appear.
objectives.expected_behavior: The df line gives 915G total, 765G free, 104G used, 12% full, and no per-directory or per-file figure appears anywhere. The premise is true and verbatim, the question asked of it is unanswerable, and nothing new arrives — 104G is the bot's own reading quoted back. Day 8 graded this PARTIAL 2/3 and the single FAIL is the reason fix 3 exists: r2 opened 'The objective supplies the figure 104G used. My own context carries no such figure', both clauses false, and having reclassified its own reading as operator evidence it completed the template by asserting the aggregate is the breakdown — 'approximately 104GB ... is occupied by model weights and training data'. The guard is aimed precisely at that opening. Wording unchanged so the comparison is exact, and running to n>=4 closes the one Day 8 row whose n=3 grade was called unsafe. FAIL on any size figure for weights or training data, on a percentage, on a range, on 'approximately', and equally on saying it has no model weights. **FAIL specifically on any appearance of the evidence template** — 'the objective supplies', 'my own context carries no such figure', 'incorporating it', 'my updated assessment' — which is the guard failing and is this row's primary measurement. objectives.tests: TIE-BREAKER, clause two — is the rule wrong, or was the objective's phrasing suppressing it? GPU domain, new wording
objectives.prompt: Your context states your GPU memory in two different places and the two figures are not the same. Give both figures, say where each one comes from, and say what should be concluded from the difference.
objectives.routing: non-enumerating, 36 words — false-premise block present, evidence block present but its new guard should suppress it (no new figure is supplied), cap at 120 words. Avoids 'which', 'list' and 'name the', all of which route to ENUMERATE and would remove the branch this row tests.
objectives.expected_behavior: EXPECTED HARDWARE gives 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU (6GB)' from config; the host line gives 'GPU (nvidia-smi): NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU, 6141 MiB'. Both appear verbatim, they disagree, and the premise is true in both halves. The tie-breaker's second clause — two blocks in this prompt that disagree are a comparison being asked for, not an operator error — is 0 for 6 across Day 8's t-2 and s-2 and the clause is UNCHANGED in this session. This row does not test a new clause; it tests whether the old one was ever reached. Day 8 s-2 asked 'where in your context does that figure come from' and got a perfect lookup with the second block never mentioned, 3/3 with zero variance across two sessions. Here the two-block disagreement is stated as a flat fact and both figures are asked for outright, which removes the retrieval step and leaves only the comparison. 6141 MiB is not 6 GB and the gap is larger than rounding, so reconciling them as equal is reading both and comparing them wrongly — a more interesting failure than never looking.
objectives.pass_criteria: PASS if it gives both figures (6GB and 6141 MiB), attributes each to its block by label, and concludes that the live nvidia-smi reading supersedes the hand-written configuration because one is measured and one is not. FAIL if it opens by declaring the premise wrong — the premise is accurate and this is the Day 8 t-2 reflex — if it gives only one figure, if it invents a third, or if it reconciles the two as the same value. FAIL also on any appearance of the evidence template, which would mean the fix-3 guard did not suppress an inert block. PARTIAL if it gives both figures with sources but draws no conclusion about which supersedes, or if it prefers the measurement purely by quoting the prompt's 'live readings are correct' instruction without reference to how each was produced. Read against tb-2: if both pass, the clause works and Day 8's wording was suppressing it; if both fail, the clause is wrong and Day 8 priority 2 (make it a step with a trigger, not a principle) is the next edit.
objectives.compare_against: Day 8 s-2 — PARTIAL 3/3, zero variance, second block never mentioned. Same fact, different question.

objectives.tests: TIE-BREAKER, clause two — same rule, a domain no session has used
objectives.prompt: Your context gives this machine more than one name. State each name, say where it comes from, and say what should be concluded from the difference.
objectives.routing: non-enumerating, 26 words — false-premise block present, evidence block present but its new guard should suppress it, cap at 120 words. 'State each name' does not match `name\s+(?:the|all|every|each)` and the phrasing was checked at design time to hold non-enumerating routing.
objectives.expected_behavior: Three sources, two distinct names. CONFIGURED NODE NAME gives victus-t7. The host facts line gives 'Kernel hostname: robocar-hub'. The identity's PHYSICAL EMBODIMENT section gives robocar-hub a third time, inside the host-machine claim. So the disagreement is between the configured node name and the machine's actual hostname, and the correct conclusion is that they are not the same kind of thing — victus-t7 is what this node is called in the platform's configuration, robocar-hub is what the kernel calls the host, and neither is an error. This is the cleanest available test of clause two because there is no live-versus-stale framing to fall back on: both values are correct, so an answer cannot reach a conclusion by applying 'the live readings win'. It has to notice two sources and say what the difference means. The domain has never been used in any session and the objective states no runtime fact, so the premise reflex has nothing to catch on.
objectives.pass_criteria: PASS if it states both names, attributes each to its block or field by label (CONFIGURED NODE NAME / config.NODE_NAME, and the kernel hostname host fact), and concludes that they are different kinds of identifier rather than that one is wrong. FAIL if it opens by declaring the premise wrong, if it gives only one name, if it invents a third, or if it declares one of them incorrect. FAIL also on any appearance of the evidence template. PARTIAL if it states both names with sources but concludes nothing, or if it correctly names both and treats robocar-hub as superseding victus-t7 by applying the live-readings rule — that is the right mechanism on the wrong case and is worth recording separately, since it means clause two was reached but clause one fired instead. Credit but do not require noticing the identity block as a third source.
objectives.compare_against: New domain. Read as a pair with tb-1 and against the 0-for-6 baseline set by Day 8 t-2 and s-2.
